scope: Union home budget — police, intelligence, investigation. The Union Expenditure Budgets (Notes on Demands for Grants, indiabudget.gov.in) read line by line: Demand 'Police' (MHA) for the CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP, SSB, Assam Rifles, NSG, Delhi Police (the one city police force with a Union demand line), Intelligence Bureau, SPG, NATGRID, J&K Police, Central Police Organisations, the Modernisation of Police Forces and Security Related Expenditure grants to States, Safe City and Nirbhaya Fund lines; the MHA demand for the IB, NCB and NIA before they moved; the Cabinet demand (total, Cabinet Secretariat line, SPG until FY2012-13) with the void that RAW is not itemised; the Enforcement Directorate (Department of Revenue demand) and the CBI (Department of Personnel and Training demand); BE, RE and actual by FY, FY1999-00 to FY2026-27, with the demand number printed in each head and the later edition's figure preferred when two editions differ (both recorded in the note). State-wise ASUMP allocation and release FY2020-21 to FY2024-25 from one Lok Sabha answer. Strength by force from PRS transcriptions of BPR&D (reported:) and the MHA Annual Report. Home Ministers 1998-2026 as dated roles. Base rates beside denominators, UPA-II beside NDA on the same lines, and three narratives on the ladder. Three levels of resolution: Union money resolves to the line item; state money resolves to the Police major head per state (and prisons per state from NCRB), with strength and per-capita figures `reported:` while BPR&D is down; city money does not exist outside Delhi Police, and city strength has no primary while BPR&D is down — cities get the footprint (installations, commissionerate entities with `reported:` strength) and the void. Left out: defence budgets (another file), State police budgets and prisons (other files), deployments and orders of battle, procurement, allegations and cases.

claims.lab: Same lens on the seven CAPF lines: UPA-II beside NDA
claims.d: Actual expenditure on the seven CAPF lines of the Police demand (CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP, SSB, Assam Rifles, NSG): ₹22,186.68 crore (FY2009-10) to ₹35,263.20 crore (FY2013-14), x1.59, 12.3% a year (nominal) over four years (UPA-II; Home Ministers P. Chidambaram then S. Shinde); ₹39,913.38 crore (FY2014-15) to ₹104,653.24 crore (FY2024-25), x2.62, 10.1% a year (nominal) over ten years (NDA; Home Ministers R. Singh then A. Shah). First four NDA years (FY2014-15 to FY2018-19): ₹39,913.38 to ₹67,560.27 crore, 14.1% a year. Union total expenditure over the same windows: 11.1% a year (₹10,24,487 to ₹15,59,447 crore) and 10.8% a year (₹16,63,673 to ₹46,52,867 crore). The line grew faster than total expenditure in UPA-II and slightly slower than it over the NDA decade; over NDA's first four years (which contain the 7th Pay Commission step) it grew faster than in UPA-II. The FY2009-10 base itself carries 6th Pay Commission arrears, which lowers the UPA-II rate. The FY2014-15 step (+13.2% on FY2013-14) falls between the two windows and is attributed to neither; counting it as NDA's (FY2013-14 to FY2024-25, eleven years) gives 10.4% a year. Audit note: the FY2009-10 base was corrected from ₹22,083.97 crore after the Assam Rifles block, split across a page in EB 2011-12, was found to have been extracted without its capital (₹102.47 crore) and plan (₹0.24 crore) lines; the other six FY2009-10 force totals were re-checked against the same edition and agree.
claims.innocentReading: These lines are mostly pay, allowances, rations and pension-linked revenue costs of forces whose size is set by battalions raised; the 6th Pay Commission arrears fall in FY2008-10 and the 7th in FY2016-17, so both governments' windows contain a pay-commission step. Nothing in the comparison implies intent; over the full windows UPA-II (12.3%) grew faster than NDA (10.1%) on this line, over NDA's first four years NDA grew faster.
claims.upgradeIf: A force-level decomposition (pay vs non-pay, new raisings) from the Detailed Demands shows a spending pattern that diverges from the pay-commission steps.
claims.killIf: The extracted actuals are shown to be mis-transcribed against the printed Notes.

claims.lab: The Police demand as a share of Union total expenditure, FY2009-10 to FY2024-25
claims.d: Police demand (net, all lines) as a share of Union total expenditure, actuals: mean 3.05% (range 2.80-3.20%) over FY2009-10 to FY2013-14 against 3.30% (range 2.61-3.96%) over FY2014-15 to FY2024-25; FY2024-25 3.15%. Year by year: 3.10, 2.80, 3.03, 3.12, 3.20 | 3.38, 3.54, 3.70, 3.82, 3.96, 3.80, 2.61, 2.81, 2.76, 2.81, 3.15. The NDA mean is driven by FY2016-17 to FY2019-20 (3.70-3.96%, the 7th Pay Commission years); FY2020-21 to FY2023-24 (2.61-2.81%) sat at or below the UPA-II low (2.80%, FY2010-11). FY2014-15 straddles both governments; leaving it out moves the NDA mean to about 3.29%. What the demand covers changed over time (SPG from FY2012-13; later BADP, RRU, NFSU, Modernisation Plan IV; J&K Police from FY2019-20), so the band is not strictly like for like. BE 2026-27: ₹173,802.53 crore = 3.25% of ₹53,47,315 crore. The seven CAPF lines alone: 2.13% (UPA-II mean; recomputed after the FY2009-10 Assam Rifles correction, 2.131%) and 2.43% (NDA mean).
claims.innocentReading: The share is flat within a 1.4-point band. The low of 2.61% (FY2020-21) is mostly a denominator effect — total expenditure jumped to ₹35,09,836 crore in the pandemic year — and the numerator fell 10% as well (₹1,02,027.49 crore to ₹91,610.65 crore; capital outlay nearly halved, ₹8,901.98 crore to ₹4,934.84 crore). Union expenditure includes transfers and interest, so the share is a crude scale, not a priority ranking.
claims.upgradeIf: A like-for-like series that excludes interest and transfers shows a sustained break.
claims.killIf: Total-expenditure denominators are shown to be revised in later Budget at a Glance editions by more than the band.

claims.lab: Delhi Police budget growth, UPA-II beside NDA
claims.d: Delhi Police actuals: ₹2,691.37 crore (FY2009-10) to ₹4,193.85 crore (FY2013-14), 11.7% a year; ₹4,616.95 crore (FY2014-15) to ₹12,133.16 crore (FY2024-25), 10.1% a year. One step: actual ₹8,015.66 crore (FY2020-21) to ₹11,131.48 crore (FY2021-22), +39% (BE 2021-22 had been ₹8,338.12 crore; RE ₹11,136.22 crore, revenue head), about 64% of it in the object head Professional Services (₹172 crore to ₹2,152 crore; purpose not stated). The Notes' description of the line does not state the reason; the MHA Detailed Demands for Grants put the revision in 2055.00.119.01.01.28 Professional Services: actual FY2020-21 ₹172.20 crore, BE 2021-22 ₹252.00 crore, RE 2021-22 ₹2,132.05 crore, actual FY2021-22 ₹2,152.16 crore, RE 2022-23 ₹1,572.00 crore; Salaries ₹6,179.93 crore to ₹6,713.98 crore. The Detailed Demands identify the head but not the purpose. BE 2026-27 ₹12,503.65 crore = 7.2% of the Police demand. Sanctioned strength 88,825 (MHA Annual Report 2017-18) and 94,257 (Annual Report 2025-26). Measurement notes: the pre-FY2015-16 figures are the sub-head .01 "Delhi Police" rather than "Total- Delhi Police" (₹2,704.31 crore FY2009-10 and ₹4,210.59 crore FY2013-14 as totals), a difference under 1%; the Police demand's FY2024-25 total includes J&K Police (₹8,553.38 crore), which, excluded, puts the demand's NDA growth at about 9.4% a year (FY2014-15 to FY2024-25) so Delhi Police grew about 0.7 points faster than the rest of the demand on that window. All rates nominal.
claims.innocentReading: The Delhi Police is the national capital's police under Article 239AA; its cost has to be met by the Union whoever governs Delhi. Its growth is within one point of the Police demand's growth in both windows; the FY2021-22 step is a single revision visible in the RE, concentrated in Professional Services per the Detailed Demands; the purpose of that head's roughly twelve-fold rise is the remaining gap, not a finding.
claims.upgradeIf: A Parliament answer, Standing Committee report or MHA outcome document states what the FY2021-22 Professional Services provision (about ₹2,132 crore RE) paid for.
claims.killIf: The step is shown to be a reclassification between demands, or Professional Services is shown to absorb a head previously booked under another demand.

claims.lab: Intelligence Bureau budget, UPA-II beside NDA
claims.d: Intelligence Bureau actuals in the Police demand: ₹874.05 crore (FY2011-12) to ₹1,050.20 crore (FY2013-14), 9.6% a year nominal; ₹1,122.97 crore (FY2014-15) to ₹4,013.19 crore (FY2024-25), x3.57, 13.6% a year nominal. Comparator: the whole Police demand grew about 12.2% a year (FY2011-12 to FY2013-14) against about 10.1% (FY2014-15 to FY2024-25), and the CRPF about 11.7% against 10.3%, so the IB pattern runs opposite to the demand's. Sensitivity: measured from the last UPA actual (FY2013-14 to FY2024-25) the NDA rate is about 13.0%; the FY2013-14 to FY2014-15 step (+6.9%) sits in neither window. BE 2026-27 ₹6,782.43 crore, of which capital ₹2,549.54 crore (RE 2025-26 capital ₹257.01 crore); the Notes give no breakdown. BE 2026-27 is +63% on RE 2025-26 (₹4,159.11 crore) and +74% on BE 2025-26 (₹3,893.35 crore). The separate Police Infrastructure line 14.01 (Building Projects of CAPFs and Central Police Organisations, ₹5,040.87 crore BE 2026-27) carries IB buildings, so the ₹2,549.54 crore is not buildings money moved across. Press reports (ThePrint, 1 Feb 2026; The Wire, Feb 2026) link the step to the 2025 Pahalgam and Red Fort attacks; no official explanation is on record. Before FY2011-12 the IB was printed in the Ministry of Home Affairs demand together with the Bureau of Immigration (FY2009-10 actual ₹878.37 crore; the 2004-05 Notes say the IB line 'also includes provision for Bureau of Immigration and Border Check Posts managed by Intelligence Bureau'), so the earlier years are not like-for-like and are not used in the growth comparison.
claims.innocentReading: The IB's line is the largest intelligence-agency line the Union itemises (the Research and Analysis Wing is not itemised); its growth is partly the Bureau's mandate and partly a one-year capital step in BE 2026-27 that the Notes do not explain (buildings and technology capital is lumpy). The comparison window for UPA-II is only two years.

claims.lab: ED budget growth beside the CBI's and the NIA's
claims.d: Actual expenditure: ED ₹35.34 crore (FY2009-10) to ₹60.57 crore (FY2013-14), x1.71 (14.4% a year), then to ₹516.09 crore (FY2024-25), x8.52 (21.5% a year over eleven years); CBI ₹386.21 crore to ₹444.24 crore (x1.15, 3.6% a year) then to ₹996.58 crore (x2.24, 7.6% a year); NIA ₹37.58 crore (FY2011-12, its first full Police-demand year) to ₹77.59 crore (FY2014-15), x2.06, after which it is not itemised (RE 2015-16 ₹92.59 crore; from FY2016-17 inside the Central Police Organisations line, ₹1,491.19 crore actual FY2024-25 for the whole line). Union total expenditure FY2013-14 to FY2024-25: x2.98 (10.4% a year). In rupees the ED's increase over eleven years is ₹455.52 crore, 0.0098% of FY2024-25 total expenditure; the ED line is 0.0111% and the CBI line 0.0214% of it. Scope: the ED figures are the revenue-only "Enforcement Directorate" establishment line (major head 2047), excluding ED capital on "Capital Outlay for Other Fiscal Services" and "Capital Outlay on Housing"; the CBI and NIA figures include capital (4055). Most of the ED step after FY2021-22 is one year: ₹306.39 crore (FY2021-22) to ₹495.48 crore (FY2022-23); in that year the demand's "Other Expenditure" line (the PMLA Adjudicating Authority and the appellate tribunals) printed nil actual (EB 2024-25, Demand 35), a possible one-year booking shift into the ED line; the level then held at ₹502.12 crore (FY2023-24) and ₹516.09 crore (FY2024-25) with the tribunals booked separately.
claims.innocentReading: The ED's growth is mandate growth on a very small base: its recorded PMLA cases (ECIRs) rose from 185 (FY2013-14) to 775 (FY2024-25) and peaked at 1,116 (FY2021-22), its searches from 46 (FY2014-15) to 2,317 (FY2024-25), it opened offices in all seven North-East states, and the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act 2018 added work; the CBI's mandate (corruption cases against public servants) did not change, and its line grew roughly with total expenditure; the NIA is a statutory agency created in 2008-09. A faster-growing line does not show the purpose for which an agency's powers are used.
claims.upgradeIf: Cost-per-case series by agency (ED, CBI, NIA) from their Annual Reports show the ED line outrunning its workload after adjusting for FEMA and FEOA work.
claims.killIf: The extracted ED or CBI actuals are shown to mix in housing capital or pension lines that changed head, or the FY2022-23 step is shown to be tribunal (AA-PMLA/ATFP) or other non-ED establishment cost booked to the ED line.

claims.lab: ED expenditure beside its recorded cases and searches (all-statute spending; FEMA/FEOA work not separated)
claims.d: Nominal ED actual expenditure per ECIR recorded: FY2013-14 ₹0.327 crore (₹60.57 crore over 185 ECIRs); FY2024-25 ₹0.666 crore (₹516.09 crore over 775 ECIRs), x2.03 (about x1.15 at constant CPI). ECIRs: x4.19; ED searches 46 to 2,317 (x50; FY2014-15 to FY2024-25 — LS USQ 1310 has no FY2013-14 figure); prosecution complaints plus supplementary: 68 (FY2014-15) to 457 (FY2024-25). The Directorate's own report: before April 2014 'only 1,883 ECIRs had been registered – averaging fewer than 200 annually'; April 2014 to March 2024: 5,113 ECIRs, 'averaging 511 annually'. Endpoint sensitivity (₹ crore per ECIR): FY2012-13 0.20, FY2015-16 0.80 (₹87.75 crore over 110), FY2018-19 1.40 (₹212.53 crore over 152), FY2021-22 0.27 (₹306.39 crore over 1,116), FY2024-25 0.67 — so "doubled" is an endpoint comparison, not a trend. The 185 ECIRs for FY2013-14 come from the ED Annual Report alone; LS USQ 1310 starts at FY2014-15.
claims.innocentReading: ECIRs are a crude workload measure: ED also runs the Foreign Exchange Management Act, the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act and attachments and restitution (₹15,261 crore restituted in 30 cases in FY2024-25 per the report), and a case's cost is dominated by search, attachment and trial work, not registration. Cost per ECIR doubling is within what a rising search count would produce.
claims.upgradeIf: ED discloses an expenditure split by statute.
claims.killIf: The ECIR counts differ between the Annual Report and the Lok Sabha answer (they agree for FY2014-15 to FY2024-25).

claims.lab: The ED line was already growing fast before FY2014-15
claims.d: ED budget estimates: BE 2000-01 ₹14.25 crore; BE 2004-05 ₹18.40 crore; BE 2013-14 ₹70.86 crore (x3.85 over nine years (ten budgets), 16.2% a year in nominal terms, UPA-I/II); BE 2014-15 ₹81.01 crore; BE 2025-26 ₹550.75 crore (x6.80 over eleven years (twelve budgets), 19.0% a year nominal, NDA); BE 2026-27 ₹594.97 crore, which makes BE 2014-15 to BE 2026-27 18.1% a year, so the 19.0% figure depends on stopping at 2025-26. Denominator: Union total expenditure (BE) grew about 14.9% a year from BE 2004-05 to BE 2013-14 (₹4,77,829 crore to ₹16,65,297 crore) and about 9.9% a year from BE 2014-15 to BE 2025-26 (₹17,94,892 crore to ₹50,65,345 crore), so the ED line ran about 1.3 points ahead of total expenditure under UPA and about 9 points ahead under NDA. The 2011 cadre restructuring (sanctioned strength 745 to 2,063 per the Directorate) fell in UPA-II. NDA-era nominal growth is faster (19.0% against 16.2% a year in budget estimates; 21.5% against 14.4% in actuals over the windows in the companion claim) and continued an earlier upward trend, but relative to total Union expenditure the gap widened from about 1 point to about 9 points a year.
claims.innocentReading: Budget estimates are not outturn; the BE series is lumpy (BE 2004-05 ₹18.40 crore, BE 2013-14 ₹70.86 crore are small numbers where one head moves the total). The rate comparison is between a nine-year and an eleven-year window. Endpoint caveat: UPA-II alone (BE 2009-10 ₹51.42 crore to BE 2013-14 ₹70.86 crore) is 8.3% a year, because BE 2009-10 overshot its actual (₹35.34 crore); the BE 2008-09 (₹27.45 crore) to BE 2009-10 jump coincides with the 6th Pay Commission.
claims.upgradeIf: A decomposition of the ED line by head (pay, office expenses, housing) shows what drove each period.
claims.killIf: The BE series is shown to include a head transfer in a particular year.

claims.lab: Capital share of the seven CAPF lines, UPA-II beside NDA
claims.d: Capital (major head 4055) as a share of the seven CAPF lines, actuals summed: FY2010-11 to FY2013-14 ₹3,048.04 crore of ₹116,729.12 crore = 2.61%; FY2014-15 to FY2024-25 ₹12,996.79 crore of ₹780,080.29 crore = 1.67%; FY2024-25 1.88%. Year by year: 3.30 (FY2010-11), 3.23, 2.42, 1.85 (FY2013-14) | 1.64, 1.65, 1.81, 2.08, 1.72, 1.73, 1.16, 1.17, 1.47, 2.03, 1.88 (FY2024-25) — the share already fell from 3.30% to 1.85% within UPA-II, and the NDA range is 1.16-2.08%, so the two period means should not be read alone. Revenue-to-capital ratio about 37:1 (UPA-II) and 59:1 (NDA). FY2009-10 is omitted: the Assam Rifles split for that year (capital ₹102.47 crore) was recovered only on audit, and the window is kept at FY2010-11. The denominator carries the pay revisions (6th CPC arrears in FY2008-10, 7th CPC from FY2016-17), which lower the capital share in those years without any change in capital spending. The year-wise force rows are in this file's budgets series, each citing the Expenditure Budget edition that prints the t-2 actual.
claims.innocentReading: Revenue is not pay alone (rations, clothing, travel, weapons maintenance) so the ratio is a revenue-to-capital ratio, not a pay-to-capital ratio; the Detailed Demands carry the pay lines. Building capital sat in separate lines in both periods: FY2011-12 actuals, Construction of Residential Accommodation for Central Police Organisations ₹607.15 crore and Construction of Buildings for Police — Central Police Organisations ₹1,760.17 crore (items 29.01 and 30.01, Demand 55, EB 2013-14); FY2024-25 actuals, Building Projects of CAPFs and Central Police Organisations ₹1,894.58 crore (item 14.01, Demand 51, EB 2026-27). Border Infrastructure capital outlay (FY2011-12 Border Management ₹992.46 crore; FY2024-25 ₹3,649.79 crore) and Modernization Plan IV (a separate line from about FY2022-23; FY2024-25 actual ₹119.24 crore; BE 2026-27 ₹343.66 crore) are likewise excluded, and their inclusion could move the comparison either way.
claims.upgradeIf: Pay & Allowances by force are extracted from the Detailed Demands and combined with the scheme capital lines.
claims.killIf: Major-head split by force is shown to be mislabelled in the Notes; or reclassification of CAPF procurement between force lines and scheme lines (MP-III/MP-IV) is shown to account for the gap.

claims.lab: Scale and composition of the CAPF lines beside Defence Services, BE 2026-27
claims.d: BE 2026-27: seven CAPF lines ₹116,587.16 crore (₹116,789.30 crore with Departmental Accounting) of which capital ₹2,302.72 crore (2.0%); Defence Services revenue (Demand 20, net) ₹365,478.98 crore plus Capital Outlay on Defence Services (Demand 21) ₹219,306.47 crore = ₹584,785.45 crore, of which capital 37.5%; defence pensions (Demand 22) are a further ₹1,71,338.22 crore. The CAPF lines are 19.9% of Defence Services revenue plus capital. Strength: 10,26,879 sanctioned CAPF posts (sum of PRS Table 4, January 2024, six forces excluding NSG; PRS's text gives "about 10.5 lakh" as of July 2024) beside a Defence Services pay-and-allowances line of ₹1,18,167.91 crore for the Army alone. Scope: the 2.0% is the equipment and vehicle capital inside the seven establishment lines. CAPF capital outside these lines in Demand 51, BE 2026-27: item 16 Modernization Plan IV for CAPFs ₹252.18 crore capital (₹343.66 crore total); item 12 BSF Air Wing ₹72.01 crore capital (₹95.05 crore total); item 14.01 Building Projects of CAPFs and Central Police Organisations ₹5,040.87 crore (shared with the IB and CPOs, not split by force); item 13.02 Border Infrastructure capital outlay ₹5,266.51 crore. Including items 12 and 16 gives about 2.2%; including all of 14.01 about 6.3% (₹7,667.78 crore of ₹1,22,066.74 crore); about 10% with border infrastructure — against 37.5% for Defence, where Demand 21 includes works capital. The CISF line (₹15,973.85 crore) is net of ₹855 crore recoveries (gross ₹16,828.85 crore), so the seven lines gross are about ₹1,17,442 crore.
claims.innocentReading: The comparison is of two budgets with different mandates: CAPFs guard borders, protect installations and assist States under MHA control; their budget is overwhelmingly revenue. A low capital share is what a force of that kind looks like and says nothing about use; it is also partly an artefact of booking — CAPF buildings and modernisation are carried in separate Demand 51 scheme lines (14.01, 16, 12, 13.02), not in the establishment lines compared here. Operational deployments are outside this file's scope.
claims.upgradeIf: Demand 51 restructures CAPF capital into the establishment lines, or a documented transfer of heavy equipment (artillery, armour, combat aircraft) into CAPF Modernization Plan lines is found in Parliament answers.
claims.killIf: Defence Services figures are revised by supplementary demands that change the ratio materially.

claims.lab: CAPF strength per lakh of population and the vacancy trend
claims.d: As on January 2024 (six forces, NSG not in the table): sanctioned 1,026,879, actual 952,764, 7.2% vacant; per lakh of projected population (14,007 lakh): 73.3 sanctioned, 68.0 actual. The same measure for all State and UT police is 155 actual (197 sanctioned) per lakh (BPR&D via PRS Table 22, January 2024; BPR&D's population base differs from the NCP projection used here for the CAPFs). Denominator: MoSPI Table 1.1 population projections, 2021 = 1,363.00 million and 2026 = 1,425.90 million, interpolated to 1,400.74 million for 2024. CAPF actual strength per lakh: 61.9 (2012), 69.1 (2014), 70.5 (2017), 67.0 (2023), 68.0 (2024). Vacancy rate as of 1 January: 14% (2012), 9% (2013), 6% (2014), 7% (2015), 7% (2016), 15% (2017; seven forces including NSG) (PRS aggregate table from BPR&D); derived from the force rows: 8.5% (2019), 10.4% (2020), 11.3% (2021), 9.3% (2023), 7.2% (2024; six forces, NSG excluded); 8.0% on 1 July 2024 (PIB) — so the series shows a 2019-21 rise and a change in force coverage, not one trend. The 2017 jump comes from sanctioned strength rising from 9.7 lakh to 10.8 lakh (new posts), not from attrition (PRS's own text says 11% for January 2019, which its rows do not reproduce); PIB: 84,106 vacancies against 10,45,751 sanctioned on 01.07.2024 (8.0%). A PIB release of a Lok Sabha reply (05.02.2019) lists vacancies by force on 01.01.2019 (CRPF 22,980; BSF 21,465; CISF 10,415; SSB 18,102; ITBP 6,643; AR 4,432; total 84,037); for BSF, SSB and Assam Rifles these equal sanctioned minus actual in the PRS January 2019 rows.
claims.innocentReading: CAPFs are a standing central pool; they are not distributed per head of population as a local police is, so the per-lakh figure is a scale, not a coverage rate. Vacancy follows recruitment cycles (UPSC/SSC), new raisings and the ex-Agniveer reservation decision; at least 8% has been vacant in every year since 2019 per PRS.
claims.upgradeIf: BPR&D Data on Police Organisations 2025 is reachable and the strength series is extended.
claims.killIf: The PRS transcription differs from the BPR&D table (BPR&D is unreachable from this sandbox).

claims.lab: The state-police modernisation grant: allocation, release and outturn
claims.d: Parliament answer (LS USQ 4862, 01.04.2025): ASUMP (the scheme formerly called MPF) allocation to States was ₹521.10 crore (FY2020-21), ₹521.10 crore, ₹437.78 crore, ₹237.50 crore and ₹482.93 crore (FY2024-25); releases ₹103.02, ₹158.39, ₹31.06, ₹45.18 and ₹96.61 crore (19.8%, 30.4%, 7.1%, 19.0%, 20.0% of allocation — a 7.1-30.4% range; FY2024-25 is as on 27.03.2025). The number of the 28 States that received nothing in a year: 16 (FY2020-21), 13 (FY2021-22), 0 (FY2022-23), 18 (FY2023-24), 13 (FY2024-25). Printed reason: release depends on utilization certificates and (from FY2024-25) the SNA-SPARSH fund-flow model; West Bengal received nothing in three of the five years (FY2020-21, FY2021-22, FY2023-24), ₹0.544 crore in FY2022-23 and ₹6.505 crore in FY2024-25; 12 of the 28 States received nothing in at least three of the five years and five States (Arunachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Manipur, Tamil Nadu) in four. Every State row is in the budgets series. Budget Estimates line "Modernisation of State Police Forces and Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS)" (which includes CCTNS, so it is not ASUMP-to-States alone): BE 2022-23 ₹621.45 crore, RE ₹152.52 crore (EB 2023-24, item 28.01), actual ₹34.72 crore (EB 2024-25, item 27.01); ASUMP releases for FY2022-23 to States plus UTs (Tables I and II) were ₹36.51 crore, against the EB actual of ₹34.72 crore on a different accounting basis. Context for FY2022-23 from the Table II note: ASUMP guidelines were circulated only on 08.08.2022 and every State received a token release that year. The UPA-II and party-split controls were not run on this line, and no West Bengal government response was found (not asked).
claims.innocentReading: The release rule is mechanical: States with unspent balances and pending utilization certificates are not eligible for the next tranche under Department of Expenditure guidelines for centrally sponsored schemes, and the answer states the rule in general terms for all States; a low release is the Union's rule meeting State accounting, not a ruling-party pattern, which this file does not test.
claims.upgradeIf: A State-by-year ruling-party table is joined to the budgets rows and the release ratio differs systematically for like-for-like unspent balances.
claims.killIf: The Annexure totals do not equal the sum of State rows (they do: all fifteen printed column totals are reproduced by the State rows).

claims.lab: PMLA convictions under two denominators
claims.d: Lok Sabha USQ 1310 (08.12.2025): from 01.04.2014 to 30.11.2025 PMLA Special Courts delivered 56 instances of judgments on merits on the money-laundering issue (the answer's wording; discharges and other non-merits disposals are not counted), convictions in 53 (121 accused): 94.64% of instances decided on merits. The same 53 convictions set against the 6,444 ECIRs recorded in the same window (FY2014-15 to 30.11.2025) are 0.82% — cohorts not matched: the government says convictions and filings "are not directly correlated", and some convictions may arise from the 1,883 pre-April-2014 ECIRs — and 2.19% of the 2,416 prosecution complaints plus supplementary complaints filed (1,843 PCs + 573 supplementary PCs, the latter filed in existing cases; 2.88% of the 1,843 main PCs). The Directorate's Annual Report 2024-25 counts, all-time ("till date", about April 2025, not from 01.04.2014), 47 cases decided, 44 convictions of 100 persons, 3 acquittals on merit, 1,739 complaints pending at various stages of trial, and itself notes that the conviction rate 'is a measure of outcomes in disposed cases, and not a ratio of convictions to total number of ongoing investigations or pending trials'.
claims.innocentReading: Both ratios are arithmetically correct and answer different questions: the first is quality of decided cases, the second is throughput of a pipeline (window-matched, not cohort-matched) most of whose cases are still in trial (PMLA trials usually await the predicate offence). Neither measures whether any particular investigation was well founded.
claims.upgradeIf: Trial-stage data by cohort year show the pending share falling or not.

narratives.claim: The ED budget exploded under the NDA.
narratives.strongestCase: The ED's actual expenditure rose from ₹60.57 crore (FY2013-14) to ₹516.09 crore (FY2024-25), x8.52 or 21.5% a year, against x2.98 (10.4% a year) for Union total expenditure and x2.24 for the CBI; BE 2014-15 ₹81.01 crore to BE 2025-26 ₹550.75 crore is x6.80. The ED's searches went from 46 (FY2014-15) to 2,317 (FY2024-25), its ECIRs from 185 to 775 (peak 1,116 in FY2021-22), and like for like the NDA-era rates exceed the UPA-era ones, all nominal: actuals 21.5% a year against UPA-II's 14.4% (FY2009-10 ₹35.34 crore to FY2013-14 ₹60.57 crore); budget estimates 19.0% (BE 2014-15 to BE 2025-26) against 16.2% (BE 2004-05 to BE 2013-14). Series: the ED revenue line (major head 2047, Department of Revenue demand); ED capital is booked under Capital Outlay for Other Fiscal Services and is excluded.
narratives.strongestCounter: The base is tiny: the ED's increase over eleven years is ₹455.52 crore, 0.0098% of FY2024-25 expenditure, and the line is 0.0111% of it. The line was already rising before May 2014 (BE 2004-05 ₹18.40 crore to BE 2013-14 ₹70.86 crore, x3.85), and the large cadre restructuring (745 to 2,063 posts) was in 2011. The ED's own report says the pre-2014 caseload was fewer than 200 ECIRs a year; but the workload series did not move with the budget: ECIRs were flat (110-187 a year) through FY2018-19 while the line rose about x3.5 (₹60.57 crore to ₹212.53 crore), then jumped from FY2019-20 (557; peak 1,116 in FY2021-22; 775 in FY2024-25) (LS USQ 1310, Annexure I; ED Annual Report 2024-25, p. 104). Sanctioned strength has not risen since 2011 (2,063 then; 2,030 now, ED Annual Report 2024-25, p. 183), so the growth is spending per post, not new posts; working strength is unreported. The Directorate's own reading is under-resourcing: no cadre review in 14 years against a DoPT norm of five (p. 183), and the cross-examiner cites the FATF Mutual Evaluation Report 2024 (para 251; not opened for this file) as calling for more ED resourcing. Convictions are 53 of 56 cases decided on merits (94.6%) but 53 of 6,444 ECIRs (0.8%) because most cases are still in trial; the budget series says nothing about how the agency's powers are used.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Cost-per-case data by statute from the ED's accounts; a decomposition of the ED line by head; a clear break in the ED's staff or office numbers that does not match the workload series; or documents tying specific budget increments to specific investigations.

narratives.claim: Delhi Police is a Union force used against the Delhi government.
narratives.strongestCase: The first half is established: the Delhi Police sits in the Union's Police demand (BE 2026-27 ₹12,503.65 crore for the Delhi Police establishment line, Demand 51 item 5, 7.2% of the demand; item 14.02 Police Infrastructure — Delhi Police is a separate ₹342.50 crore, ₹12,846.15 crore for the two lines together), is headed by a Commissioner reporting to the Ministry of Home Affairs, and the Constitution (Article 239AA(3)(a)) excludes police and public order from the Delhi Assembly; the Supreme Court in 2023 quoted the 2018 Constitution Bench that this exclusion extends to executive power. The elected Delhi government therefore has no control over the force policing its capital. The "used against" half concerns the AAP-run periods (28 Dec 2013 to 14 Feb 2014; Feb 2015 to Feb 2025); from February 2025 the Union and Delhi governments are both BJP-run. The accusing side is a named party: AAP spokesperson Saurabh Bhardwaj called the Delhi Police the "armed wing of BJP" (Outlook/IANS, 5 Nov 2019).
narratives.strongestCounter: The arrangement is constitutional and dates from 1991, the same under UPA-II and NDA; its cost grew roughly in line with the Police demand (nominal actuals): 11.7% against 11.9% a year in UPA-II (FY2009-10 to FY2013-14) and 10.1% against 10.1% over FY2014-15 to FY2024-25 (10.1% against 10.3% measured from the last UPA actual, FY2013-14); excluding J&K Police, which entered the demand from FY2019-20, the rest of the demand grew 9.4% (or 9.7%) a year, so Delhi Police was about 0.4-0.7 points faster; Delhi is the seat of the national government, which is the stated rationale. Nothing in the budget, strength or court records in this file shows the force being 'used against' the Delhi government; that part of the claim is a statement about specific cases, which this file does not examine and which the evidence-auditor has not cleared. No Delhi Police or MHA response to the "armed wing" assertion was found, and neither was asked for this file; if any part of the claim is promoted to alleged it needs that contra.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Court records (orders, FIRs, chargesheets with stage and outcome) of specific proceedings, set beside the same lens run on the control: Union-controlled police in other Union Territories with legislatures (J&K UT Police under the Reorganisation Act 2019 as the structural comparator), and Union–Delhi disputes under NDA-I (1998-2004: the Vajpayee government and Home Minister Advani against Sheila Dikshit's Congress government) and the January 2014 Kejriwal dharna against the UPA-II Home Ministry. "Used against" is not promoted without court records (orders, FIRs and chargesheets with stage and outcome).

narratives.claim: The CAPFs are being used as a parallel army.
narratives.strongestCase: The CAPFs are large and border-facing: 10,26,879 sanctioned posts (sum of PRS Table 4, January 2024, six forces excluding NSG; PRS's text gives about 10.5 lakh as of July 2024), ₹116,587.16 crore in BE 2026-27 for the seven lines, 2.2% of Union expenditure, and three of them (BSF, ITBP, Assam Rifles) are border-guarding forces; ex-Agniveers are reserved 10% of constable posts (50% in the BSF from December 2025, by a gazette amendment of the BSF General Duty Cadre (Non-Gazetted) Recruitment Rules, 2015), linking the two services' recruitment.
narratives.strongestCounter: The money does not look like an army's: the seven CAPF lines are 19.9% of Defence Services revenue plus capital in BE 2026-27 and only 2.0% of the seven establishment lines is capital — the equipment and vehicle capital inside those lines; the same demand carries CAPF capital in item 14.01 Building Projects of CAPFs and CPOs (₹5,040.87 crore, BE 2026-27), item 16 Modernization Plan IV (₹252.18 crore capital), item 12 BSF Air Wing (₹72.01 crore capital) and item 13.02 Border Infrastructure (₹5,266.51 crore), which adjusted gives about 6.3% (₹7,667.78 crore of ₹1,22,066.74 crore) or about 10% with border infrastructure, against 37.5% for Defence Services, where Demand 21 includes capital works (EB 2026-27, Demand 51); the Police demand's share of Union expenditure stayed in a 2.6-4.0% band over sixteen years (FY2009-10 to FY2024-25 actuals; the seven CAPF lines alone 2.1-2.4% as period means), though the demand's composition changed (J&K Police added from FY2019-20) so the band is not strictly like for like; the seven CAPF lines grew 12.3% a year under UPA-II against 10.1% under NDA (nominal actuals), so the forces did not accelerate; the CAPFs sit under the Ministry of Home Affairs by statute with an internal-security and border-guarding mandate. Operational use and deployment are outside this file's scope and are not assessed.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Documented transfers of heavy equipment or of operational control from the services to CAPFs; a Parliament answer on CAPF deployment under army command; capital lines for CAPFs that approach the defence capital share.

symmetryCheck: Union control, run on the same lines with the same fields: UPA-II (FY2009-10 to FY2013-14) beside NDA (FY2014-15 to FY2024-25), actuals. Seven CAPF lines 12.3% a year against 10.1% (FY2009-10 base corrected on audit; the UPA-II CAPF share of Union expenditure recomputes to 2.13%, unchanged at two decimals) (Union total expenditure 11.1% against 10.8%); Police demand share of Union expenditure mean 3.05% against 3.30%; CAPF capital share 2.61% against 1.67% (actuals), and in budget estimates 2.66% (BE 2013-14: ₹898.39 crore of ₹33,733.82 crore) beside 1.98% (BE 2026-27: ₹2,302.72 crore of ₹116,587.16 crore), the seven establishment lines only; Delhi Police 11.7% against 10.1%; Intelligence Bureau 9.6% (two years) against 13.6%; ED 14.4% against 21.5% (FY2013-14 to FY2024-25); CBI 3.6% against 7.6%; CAPF vacancy rate 14%, 9%, 6% in January 2012 to 2014 against 15% (2017) falling to 7% (2024). Reading: the lines that grew faster under NDA than under UPA-II are the ED, the CBI and the IB; the forces (CAPFs, Delhi Police) did not, and the ED line was already growing at 16% a year in nominal budget estimates before FY2014-15 (though relative to total Union expenditure the gap widened from about 1 point to about 9 points a year; see c036). The PMLA pipeline lens (c041) applied to the UPA-era base — 1,883 ECIRs before April 2014 with near-zero convictions — gives the same or a lower conviction-to-ECIR ratio, so that lens is not partisan, so the lens gives a mixed picture, not an alarming one for the forces and a real acceleration on the three agency lines from small bases. Date test applied: no ED, CBI or NIA budget is attached to a Home Minister because those agencies are not in the MHA; FY2014-15 and FY2019-20 lines fall across a change of Home Minister and are attributed to neither. The States control (BJP-run beside opposition-run) is not run in this file: the State-wise ASUMP rows carry no ruling-party field and the party-by-year table is not sourced here, so the one State-level fact (zero-release counts by State) is left unsplit for the states agent. Vendor and case controls (Bofors beside Rafale, AgustaWestland beside Tatra) do not apply to this domain.

gaps: MPF/SRE lines FY2009-10 to FY2014-15 (and SRE before FY2009-10): sub-heads under 'Assistance to States' change between Expenditure Budget editions; extract by hand from the PDFs listed in sources.
Pay & Allowances by force (Detailed Demands for Grants, Finance Division page of mha.gov.in to 2012-13; later years only in the Notes) are not extracted; no pay-to-capital ratio is written.

Union total expenditure actuals before FY2009-10 and for FY2005-06 to FY2008-09 are not in this file (Budget at a Glance for FY2008-09 to FY2010-11 and FY2000-01 to FY2003-04 did not resolve); shares of Union expenditure before FY2009-10 are not stated. GDP shares are given only for BE years with the Budget's own GDP projection and are not a consistent series (the GDP base changes between 2004-05 and 2011-12 base years).

BPR&D Data on Police Organisations is unreachable: CAPF strength by force is PRS-transcribed for January 2019, 2020, 2021, 2023 and 2024 (no 2022 table found); the 2021 SSB row equals the 2020 SSB row and may be a carry-over; PRS's own Total rows are not used. The July 2026 Rajya Sabha CAPF vacancy answer was not located as a primary PDF (the sansad.in file path AU348 failed, and the MHA mirror path for that date was not found).

Per-force sanctioned strength for CRPF and SSB as on 31.12.2024 is not written because the Annual Report prints 'strength of the Force' without saying whether sanctioned or actual; actual strength by force after January 2024 is not available from a primary record.

Home Minister dates are from the Wikipedia list of Home Ministers (secondary); the Gazette notifications of appointment were not opened. Persons are recorded only in the Home Minister role; Home Secretaries and agency heads are not recorded.

The ED cadre restructuring announced in 2026 (press reports of sanctioned strength rising from about 2,029 to 3,256 posts) was not verified from a primary document and is not used. ED cases against politicians (a Deccan Herald report of 19 March 2025 on a Parliament answer: 193 cases in FY2015-16 to FY2024-25 with two convictions) could not be verified from the answer itself (the page body was behind a paywall) and is not used.
The Delhi Police FY2021-22 step (actual ₹8,015.66 crore to ₹11,131.48 crore) is unexplained in the lines read; the Delhi Government's own police-related budget is not read.
Intelligence Bureau BE 2026-27 capital ₹2,549.54 crore (RE 2025-26 ₹257.01 crore): no explanatory note in the Notes; a Parliament answer or Standing Committee report would be the place to look.

The sansad.in Lok Sabha question API was used to list MHA questions on CAPFs for the 18th Lok Sabha (sessions 1-8); the Rajya Sabha API was not tried. Several Lok Sabha answers on CAPF modernisation (USQ 3700 of 12.08.2025, USQ 2637 of 04.08.2026) were found on the MHA mirror but not read for budget data.

The Cabinet demand rows record the whole demand; the pre-2016 'Cabinet Secretariat' sub-line (inside Council of Ministers) and the National Security Council Secretariat line are not extracted as separate rows.

Entity ids: the inventory carries ngo:intelligence-bureau for the IB; this file uses ngo:intelligence-bureau per the fleet coordination list and flags the merge. force:cbi, force:enforcement-directorate, force:drdo-type nodes defined in money-people.json are defined again here with this domain's facts; the assembler should merge by id.

Headquarters (st) is set only where the Annual Report states it (BSF New Delhi, Assam Rifles Shillong); other forces' headquarters are not asserted. Footprint rows are three: one per documented place, none for deployments or battalions (out of scope).

Narrative "Delhi Police is a Union force used against the Delhi government": the accusing side is recorded (AAP, Saurabh Bhardwaj, Outlook/IANS 5 Nov 2019); no Delhi Police or MHA response was found and neither was asked for this file.
Narrative "The CAPFs are being used as a parallel army": no named proponent or circulating source was found; the narrative is recorded as circulating without a cited proponent.

PMLA convictions (c041): a Rajya Sabha answer of 04.08.2026 (MoS Pankaj Chaudhary to V. Sivadasan) reportedly gives FY2025-26 ECIRs of 1,080 and updated conviction counts, with press summaries disagreeing (56 convictions/124 accused as of 31.03.2026 in one; 43 cases/104 persons in The Wire); the RS PDF was not located and no figure from it is used.
Home Minister dates (c002): the audit names Sify and IBNLive reports of the 30 Nov 2008 resignation on web.archive.org, which is blocked from this environment; not opened, not cited.

Budgets series, pre-2016 editions: the FY2009-10 Assam Rifles block in EB 2011-12 was extracted without its capital and plan lines because the block crosses a page; the other six FY2009-10 force totals were re-checked and agree, but the FY2010-11 to FY2014-15 actuals in EB 2012-13 to EB 2016-17 have not been re-checked for the same page-break fault.
